observations.seen: Flat, even illumination across the infield in all four stadiums. There is no readable key direction from a 55° flood rig. Midtown gets a magenta tint, but the light has no falloff or pooling.
The players cast almost no contact shadows on the dirt. The batter and catcher look like they float. The mound and bases have no grounding occlusion.
No specular response on helmets, bats or bases. Uniforms and dirt read as fully diffuse, with no environment reflection.

Each venue is distinct: Harbor has a rock wall and pergolas, Canyon has giant boulders, Midtown has a skyline. However, the backdrops are low-detail billboards and the crowds are rows of colored blocks.
Midtown shows faint rain streaks. Otherwise there is no distance haze or arena volumetrics, so the outfield wall is as crisp as the infield.
The dirt has a noisy, tiled-looking procedural texture that turns into blotchy magenta in Midtown. The turf is flat green with no mowing pattern. The rocks have decent albedo but look stretched.
Fielders are generic low-poly identical figures. The outfielders are tiny white sprites. The bat is a simple cylinder. The mound is a plain disc.
The behind-the-plate broadcast view centers the diamond well. The batter and catcher occupy a small lower portion, and a large empty dirt area dominates the middle of the frame.
A high elevated perspective, not orthographic. The FOV looks wider than 40, which distorts the infield shape. The framing is consistent across frames.
There is mild vignette and grading per venue. There is no bloom on the scoreboards or lights, and frame 1 has a gray washed-out haze over the HUD region.
Static stances across frames. The only change is the batter's bat pose, and fielders show no ready-position variation.
The scoreboard, count, outs and bases panels are clean and legible. The control-hint bar is clear. The timing reticle ring is readable. The top nav bar feels like debug chrome and crowds the view.
